rationale: Classical clinical diagnostic criteria for Loeys-Dietz syndrome (LDS) across causative genes—including SMAD2 (LDS6)—state that the absence of ectopia lentis is a hallmark differentiating LDS from Marfan syndrome (FBN1). However, comprehensive reviews of published LDS cohorts (e.g., Gouda et al., 2022) note associations and reported presentations of ectopia lentis across LDS types including SMAD2, indicating that ectopia lentis may rarely occur or be misattributed in broader connective tissue phenotype overlaps, challenging its absolute utility as an infallible rule-out criterion.

evidence.text: Absence of ectopia lentis is highlighted as a primary distinguishing feature separating Loeys-Dietz syndrome (which encompasses SMAD2 mutations) from Marfan syndrome, though very few SMAD2 mutation-positive cases had initially been characterized in detail.

conflicts: Established diagnostic dogma asserts that ectopia lentis is universally absent across all LDS subtypes (including SMAD2/LDS6), whereas systematic reviews synthesizing all published clinical cases (e.g., Gouda et al., 2022) document ectopia lentis appearing in reported cohorts of SMAD2/LDS cases.

new_directions.question_text: Are individual reports of ectopia lentis in SMAD2/LDS patients confirmed by slit-lamp ophthalmologic examination, or do they represent misdiagnosed lens subluxation/myopic spherophakia?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying ophthalmologic documentation in the primary cases cited by systematic LDS meta-analyses will determine if ectopia lentis truly occurs in SMAD2-mediated disease or reflects diagnostic misclassification.
